newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - One-offs to tame Tarmac H1 profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - One-offs to tame Tarmac H1 profit.

text.p: Building group Tarmac Plc is expected to see a fall in underlying half year pretax profits next Tuesday, with the results pushed into a sharp loss once one-off charges have been taken into account.

Excluding estimates of charges, analysts' forecasts for the interim pretax profits range from six million stg to twenty million, with most predictions centred around the 15 million mark. That compares with 29.1 million in profits last year.
The interim dividend is expected to remain at the 1995 level of 3.0 pence per share.
Analysts expect the losses to partly stem from recent restructuring andits housing unit's loss, in particular.
This loss relates to a period just before an asset swap with George Wimpey Plc earlier this year, when Tarmac acquired Wimpey's aggregates and construction unit.
UBS analyst Simon Brown said he expected a pretax loss of 20 million, after accounting for charges, or a 17.5 million profit excluding them.
He said the update was likely to be "pretty dire...downbeat about the UK, but the US should be better."
UBS is a seller of Tarmac shares.
Another analyst, who is predicting a pretax, pre-exceptional profit of 20 million stg was equally downbeat about the results.
"Everyone knows the results will be a disaster in the first half," he said.
The now-sold housing unit is expected to notch up a six and a half million charge alone, he said.
Aggregates is also expected to suffer from the UK's squeeze on infrastructure spending, particulary on the roads side.
But he predicted a more upbeat scenario for construciton business, expecting near-record orders.
